@@118648275 <h> Why govt must revive grazing reserves -- Niger commissioner <p> The Niger State Commissioner for Pastoral and Nomadic Affairs , Rabe Sanda , in this interview with CHIKA OTUCHIKERE , talks about the severe impact of banditry and cattle rustling on the region , its effects , and the potential revenue from the Federal Government 's intervention in beef production <p> What are the major challenges facing pastoralists in Niger State ? <p> In the last eight years , the North has lost over 50 per cent of its cattle . Yes , we lost over 50 per cent of our cattle because of the cattle movement . Banditry and rustling are also responsible for some of these deaths . Some of them died because of the hazards of movement . There is also contributory negligence . How long are we going to continue managing this situation ? Some of them today find themselves in a situation where they do n't even have the livestock again . We need to provide alternatives so that we can accommodate our different cultures peacefully . <p> The government is not fulfilling its role , and the pastoralists are also not engaging with government policies . Many are unaware of these policies and lack access to crucial information , which is another contributing factor . There is also the rustling . A lot of people are into rustling and a lot of herders lost their cows to rustling . The government does n't pay much attention to the plight of herders . They do consider farming activities but no single support is coming from the Federal Government to the livestock and the cattle herders . With the advent of the Ministry of Livestock Development , I am telling you , it is a new Nigeria . As far as they can make use of the blueprint available to them , a new Nigeria is possible . Livestock rearing has been commercialised already . A lot of intellectuals would participate and the pastoralists would be integrated . There will be no more trouble . <p> So , what were your major challenges in the last year as commissioner ? <p> The major challenge is the level of understanding . Even our elites have limitations in their understanding because our people do not care to ask questions . The Fulani people are timid . They are always isolating themselves . So , if you want to know them more , you must draw closer to them , you must talk to them and that is the method I used . I drew them closer to myself . I adopted an open policy in running the office . If you come here , I do n't care who you are , but I must see you as far as I am on the seat . I will listen to you , so anybody coming here will not entertain the fear that he may not see me . If you come to the office , as far as the commissioner is in the office , you will see him . Another challenge is understanding the ministry . When we came on board , many people did not understand the wisdom behind the creation of this ministry . They saw it in different ways but gradually , we are talking to them , we are using different media and we are meeting different calibre of people . Thank God now the people understand better the reason behind the creation of the ministry . A lot of people abandoned the pastoralists , nobody cared about their welfare , nobody cared for them , and they did n't have a sense of belonging . That is why there are a lot of troubles today , as well as retaliations . Since we came on board , no single retaliation has been recorded in this ministry . The herders and farmers crises is real . Let me tell you , all the crises are taking place because of the destruction of farms since there are no selected areas for their cattle to graze . We have measures put in place to handle all the reports in different Local Government Areas . There are different communities which we are handling and the traditional institutions are participating alongside the stakeholders . This rainy season is the most peaceful rainy season we have witnessed in Niger State . <p> But there have been issues of farmers-herders clashes in the state , leading to loss of lives in one of the Local Government Areas ... <p> Where ? You do n't know the place ? Which local government ? I am from Niger State and I am a commissioner . The crisis in Bosso Local Government Area was not a farmers-herders clash , it was a vigilante-herders clash . There was no single reason for the killings . We do n't have a single casualty in Niger State as far as the farmers-herders clash is concerned . Here in Niger , there is no anti-grazing law . We never demarcated a portion of land for herders to graze their cattle . We are operating open grazing in the state , although we have measures , and if the herders destroy any farm , we have a committee that will go there , reconcile and pay the farmer . So far , there are no casualties in Niger State , we do n't have anyone . <p> But there are still cattle roaming in the state , even in Minna , the state capital ... <p> It is fashion . Even in Minna , we have them . We are working on the data now . After the data , we will know the number of livestock we have , we will know the portion of land we need . We must be scientific ; we ca n't say we need 10 hectares when we do n't know the number of livestock . We must know the number of livestock we have , then we prepare the ground for them . So , the number of livestock and the number of hectares that will accommodate them will be in our budget . Then we take some of our youths for training on how to develop animal husbandry . We will take it as a business and have cattle that we might develop and sell . It is a gradual process and it is not a single-day initiative , it is not magic . We are working towards that and we are achieving what we want . I came on board on August 30 , 2023 . From September to December last year , we recorded 13 casualties . This year , there is zero casualty . I want you to go and ask everywhere . No local government has recorded a single casualty or a clash between farmers and herders . What we have is the encroachment of livestock into the farms . Every day I have a lot of cases to handle . We , however , collaborate with the traditional institution and all the stakeholders in Niger State and we are responding very quickly . We have a quick response mechanism . You report today and in the next one hour , we act because we have a committee . We send them there , we have motorcycles , they will go there and check and settle whatever is happening . It is the cattle that are moving , the farm is in one place . You ca n't destroy somebody 's crop and start claiming right , you do n't have any right to claim . You have to beg him for forgiveness and pay compensation . That is the measures and we have a policy document now that we shall soon present to the council for the approval of the governor . It will bring about law and order in Niger State . You must pay when you destroy any farm and the traditional institutions will take the full position of the law . You are under them and you are answerable to them . Local governments will take full responsibility for their locality and full responsibility for their communities . <p> Do you think this cattle roaming will ever stop in Niger State ? <p> That is what we are advocating , not only in Niger State but in the whole of Nigeria . We are advocating for the clustering and the grazing reserves . Let 's have specific designated places for grazing reserves -- from this place to this place is for cattle . All the facilities will be provided there -- schools , hospitals , veterinary , dams , and boreholes -- for their well-being . Any farmer that goes there to farm knows he is the one encroaching . If he moves his cattle from the reversed areas to the farmland , he is committing a punishable offence . He will pay and will also be punished . But this is not a single day 's job . Everybody needs to come on board and let 's do it together . This livestock , we need them and we need to participate in the policymaking so that we can finally end the crisis . As long as the animals are roaming on the streets , we 'll continue to manage the crisis . So , it is a gradual process , we ca n't do it in a single night . <p> Do you recall that the Federal Government advocated open grazing and ranching ? <p> You know it is short-term planning and long-term planning . The short-term planning is that you gazette the cattle routes so that you can pave the way for them , it 's one of the challenges . You block this way today , they know this is the route that they do follow , you 're talking about animals . Even if you put farms there , they will crush it and follow that route . They will graze and drink water . You block a drinking point for them where they go and drink water in the river , you block there and put rice there or any crops , they 'll go there and drink their water , they do n't care . What the Federal Government is saying is that it is a long-term process . There is short-term planning and long-term planning . The short-term plan gives an enabling environment for them to graze , then gradually let 's keep putting our facilities , let 's prepare our grazing reserves , let 's revive our grazing reserves . Then we keep moving them , evacuating them gradually . Maybe , for the first year and the second year , there may be continuous roaming , but we continue to reduce the cattle pressure then the third , and fourth year , no more livestock in the streets again as they go into the grazing reserves . If you do n't want to go to the grazing reserves , then domesticate them , get your farms and clustering in one place . It is a business , let 's commercialise it , that is what I am advocating . Let 's move from cultural rearing to commercial rearing . You make more profit and also there will be peace . You 'll love each other because the pastoralists and the farmers do n't have problems . The common problem between the herders and the farmers is the destruction ; that is what is causing this trouble . As far as the livestock are no longer on the streets , what is the cause of the trouble again ? Everybody will be peaceful . <p> Are you saying it is more profitable to go into full-time ranching than half-way ranching and half-way grazing ? <p> Yes , full-time ranching is more profitable . When we are talking about food and profit , we must talk about our safety too . Full-time ranching will be safer . The government will provide agro rangers and the security agencies will be there so that they will protect the lives and property because they know the location . The cattle and herders are not moving , they are in one place . It is better but we do n't expect to do it in a single night . We need to keep progressing gradually , from one stage to another and finally , we will get there . That is where we are heading , ultimately . <p> Does the government collect taxes from pastoralists ? <p> That is what we are doing next after the data collection . Having known the number of livestock we have in Niger State , the location of our pastoralists and their leadership , the next thing is to have the order of animal heads and security . If you need to rear cattle in Niger State you will register and get the permit . The way you register your vehicles is the way you will register your cattle . The government will check your ranch , they will give you a permit , they will allow you to trade , it 's a business . The government will get revenue and will use the revenue to build more and more ranches and facilities for the livestock . The money will help a lot , the revenue will help , and it will even help the government to coordinate , secure the environment , secure the livestock and the owners of the livestock . It will also help to provide a lot of facilities for the owners . <p> A major issue is the child herders who grew up moving from place to place . How do you plan to address this ? <p> When you are talking about culture , you must understand that it is hereditary . Moving the cattle from place to place is now seen as part of their culture . They see it as a way of rearing their cattle . The question you will ask is , ' what is making them move to the extent that it is now a part of their habit ? They are moving because they are searching for water and green pastures where they can graze the animals . That is why I brought up the issue of pasture development as one of the important aspects of this project . As long as you continue integrating their knowledge , giving them alternatives , instead of them moving from here to Lokoja , trekking , searching for water and green pasture , this is how you provide your feed for your livestock , stay in one place . When you start with phase one , phase two will be watching , they will see how you are succeeding , they will see how phase one is enjoying and living comfortably , their children are attending schools , they 're getting more milk and making more profit than before , they are safe and they have so much care from the government . You do n't need to invite them ; they will come by themselves even with their money so that the government can do it for them . You do n't need to waste your time ; anything that is worth doing at all is worth doing well . I am very sure that when they are tired of the movement , they will come . This movement is tormenting their lives . They suffer a lot of setbacks because of this movement . We lost almost 50 per cent of our cattle because of this movement , as I said before . How long are we going to continue managing this situation ? We need to provide alternatives so that we can accommodate our culture peacefully . So , this is the way we can accommodate it . I talk to them , I show them examples . I have livestock in my house , they come and see , they know my own is better than their own , my children are attending schools , and my family is happy , you understand . So , gradually , with the support of the government , they will adopt it and they will continue with it . <p> How does the state government hope to derive maximum benefits from cattle rearing ? <p> You know , the governor just established the agro-processing zone . I had a meeting with Niger Foods in connection with a lot of stakeholders . So , what we are trying to do is to put things together to make sure we create a long value chain from the production to the end users . His Excellency is on top of the situation . I 'm telling you , even yesterday , we went to the Emir of Minna palace for stakeholders ' engagement . We discussed in detail the value chain and how we are going to make use of all the parts of our production , from the beginning to the end in Niger State . The government is preparing the ground for them . I am telling you , very soon , Niger State will start slaughtering over 1,000 cows a day for local consumption and export . <p> Climate change is one of the major factors affecting the livestock industry . What will the government do about this ? <p> Climate change caused all the hazards . When I was growing up around Minna , there were a lot of grasses and leaves that livestock could eat . One , they are medicinal and herbal . They were also a feed that provided nutrients for their body , giving enough milk in their bodies . But there are none of them today . None of the grasses are available today and none of the trees are available today because of climate change . The availability of water is no longer there . About 10 years ago , after the rainy season , nearby rivers would still have water , let 's say the whole six months of the dry season , anywhere you go , you would see water . The livestock will go to the drinking point , drink water and go . And they were very clean water . The plantations surrounding the water were flourishing . The water was very cool , even human beings would like to drink the water . But today , the plantations protecting the water are no longer there , the water is not even there , and everywhere has dried up completely . The plantations they were feeding on before are no longer available . Now , the animals are feeding on sand and sand is accumulating in their stomachs , causing a lot of trouble . They are also taking a lot of insects into their stomachs and it is killing them . So , climate change is the number one factor that caused most people to lose their livestock today . If you talk to the professionals about this , they will elaborate more about the damage of climate change , not only to the livestock but to human beings and crop production . None of the organisations that are saddled with the responsibility of tackling climate change are contacting pastoralists , because nobody cared but today , all the attention of the specialists and professionals is coming back to this field of livestock . That is why I can see the solution coming soon to Nigeria . <p> Do you think there are enough veterinary doctors for livestock in Niger State ? <p> We have a lot of veterinary doctors and facilities too , even the governor recently directed the Ministry of Nomadic and Pastoral Affairs to enlist some veterinary doctors for employment so that they would be able to handle and guide the policies . This is because , in the absence of these veterinary doctors , a lot of damage would happen , so he directed the ministry to submit the list of vet doctors for employment , which we did . We are expecting their employment letters . They are very important and we have the facilities , but it is restricted within the cities . If not for the advent of this ministry , not all of them cared to ask about the pastoralists who are major cattle owners in the rural areas . But with this ministry now , every month , every day we are in touch with them . We continue to make sure that everybody keys into the policies of the government so that they can benefit from the vaccines , the drugs and even the salt that the cattle need , it has a lot of advantages . We are not conscious of what we are consuming . <p> Do we have veterinary doctors available , as there is a dearth of medical doctors and nurses in the country ? <p> Yes , they are jetting out of the country to greener pastures but the veterinary doctors are here . Well , maybe there is a higher demand for medical doctors than veterinary doctors and veterinary doctors may have a lot of patronage in Nigeria than other countries . It might be vice versa , that is why they remain , but I know we have veterinary doctors . They 're not enough but we have them . They are taken care of in the urban cities . You know the problem is that there is a huge gap between the rural and urban cities . There is a communication gap between the circle of elite and the circle of rural dwellers or settlers , but with the creation of the Ministry of Nomadic and Pastoral Affairs , we are bridging that gap . If there is any outbreak , they report it to us . If they discover any symptoms they do not understand , they report to us . We enlighten them , we sensitise them , and we even give them room for discussion , so they are happy about it and we are solving a lot of problems . <p> How far will you say you have bridged the gap between the Fulani community and the state government ? <p> Let me tell you , 70 per cent . We have bridged the gap by 70 per cent . Everybody has access to this ministry . We do n't care where you come from , if you call our attention , in person or through delegation , we answer you . We will tell you that you are important to us . We are always ready for that . We work round the clock , including at night . We respond to calls , we respond to text messages and we answer anywhere and at any time so that we make sure they benefit from the ministry . We provide a lot of solutions . <p> What are your goals for the ministry ? <p> The short term is to coordinate the activities of our pastoralists in all their locations , data and the number of their livestock . Then we plan for them to connect with the ministry directly so that they have access to us and we have access to them . We will share privileged information . Any complaint they have , they will come to us . Those are our short-term plans . They do n't need to take the laws into their own hands . Our long-term plans are to make society in general understand and know the importance of participating in livestock and cattle rearing . We want people to see it not as Fulani business alone but as Nigerian business , a big business that everybody needs to key into because it is very profitable . I do n't know who can survive without eating beef or taking milk . So , we want to move it from cultural business to commercial business . Again , we want to move from roaming cattle on the street to a cluster or permanent place where everybody will know this is a grazing area . We want to catch our young ones and get them to start learning in their primary schools , not only to take care of cattle but how to explore other areas of the business . It is a big market , so the question should be : how to get the biggest profit from it and create a lot of employment for people ? <p> Would you say that non-Fulani residents have embraced the business of cattle rearing ? <p> It is one of our plans . We are talking to them , we are telling them the benefits of being involved in the business . For instance , if you have five goats and one he-goat , in less than a year , they could become 30 and a place like this office can accommodate the business . It is a business , it 's a side hustle , you need only one hour or two hours from your time . In the morning , you feed them , give them water and leave for your work and in the evening when you come back , you give them water , give them food and that is all . We need milk , we need cheese and we need butter . Even the dung of the cattle , we need it for manure . We need to commercialise it , make it a real manure , an organic manure instead of chemicals . Let 's keep using it for our vegetables , for our fruits and food . It will add a lot of value to our production . Today , we are not able to export because we are not producing quality foods for countries that require them and the problem is the chemicals . As long as the institutions are accommodating these feeds , and teaching the students , they 'll take advantage of it . See a lot of cattle dung in different locations , they will mop it and make it a business . For the milk , they will collect it , process and separate it . They will get cheese , butter , yoghurt and fresh milk . If you have it today people will come to your domain and buy it because people need it . It 's medicine , it is food . Everybody needs it , children and adults alike . So , as far as we can take advantage of it , if we can key into it , a lot of jobs will come out from there and it will graduate a lot of people and make them financially independent . By then , nobody will see it as a threat again . In the past , people used to see it as a threat , " Fulani man is there , he will kidnap us , he will kill us " . A lot of people who are not Fulani are into the business of kidnapping . We should cancel this idea of tribes in the issue of security . Anybody who is a criminal is a criminal , let 's declare him as a criminal , no matter where he comes from . No crime is connected with any tribe , let 's abolish that idea . We should not politicise the issue of crime or insecurity . Let us see Nigeria as Nigeria for all . Let us see how we are going to make Nigeria better , let 's see how we are going to accommodate our community and society and integrate our schools from reading and learning alone into skills acquisition centres . <p> What advice would you give the Federal Government , especially on the livestock ministry ? <p> My advice is simple . The Federal Government should not warehouse the ministry in its pocket . Some aides and intellectuals should not warehouse the ministry into their pockets . The ministry is a missionary ministry , for solutions . Let them see it as a solution-oriented ministry to provide solutions for all Nigerians and our problems , ranging from insecurity to day-to-day activities . As long as they can see it like that , they will be accepted everywhere worldwide . But when you have selfish interests and start using nepotism , ethnicity or religion , they are going nowhere . A lot of ministries , some created for over 12 , and 13 years , but nobody knows about them because of selfish interests and greed . They are not transparent and they do n't open up what they are into . What are they hiding ? Is it a cult group ? If you know you are working in the interest of Nigerian society , open it and let everybody see what you are doing and participate . Any activity , any policy , publish it let everybody see where they can participate . Let them allow the Nigerian youths to participate . If you come from the South , East or any part of the country , let the Nigerian youths see the ministry as an avenue for job creation . <p> All rights reserved . @@118648972 <h> UK : Experts warn drivers against using ' ghost ' number plates <p> Experts have raised alarms over the growing use of illegal " ghost plates " by drivers in the United Kingdom to evade speed cameras and traffic enforcement . <p> According to GBNews , recent estimates suggest that one in 15 motorists is using anti-ANPR ( Automatic Number Plate Recognition ) technology to dodge fines and charges . <p> The trend involves equipping vehicles with " invisible " licence plates designed to escape detection by speed and bus lane cameras . These illegal plates , also known as 3D or 4D number plates , utilise reflective materials and intricate designs to confuse camera systems . Additionally , some drivers distort their registration numbers with reflective tape or purchase " stealth plates " online . <h> Related Posts <p> Professor Fraser Sampson , former Biometrics and Surveillance Camera Commissioner has drawn attention to the issue , stating in a resignation letter to former Transport Secretary Mark Harper that the manipulation of number plates is widespread . <p> He warned , " For all its technological advancement and operational indispensability , the ANPR system still relies ultimately on a piece of plastic affixed to either end of a vehicle . " <p> Professor Sampson described the system 's vulnerabilities as " staggeringly simple , " particularly given the unregulated market for number plates , which enables the proliferation of stealth plates and cloned registrations . <p> Wolverhampton City Council has emerged as a frontrunner in tackling the problem , becoming the first local authority to invest in cutting-edge technology designed to detect such illegal plates . Enforcement officers are now equipped with advanced cameras capable of identifying vehicles using deceptive number plates . <p> Councillor Craig Collingswood , the cabinet member for environment and climate change , stated , " Wolverhampton is leading the way as the first council investing in this state-of-the-art technology to deter and detect offenders . " <p> Drivers caught using ghost plates face a ? 100 penalty , and licensed taxi drivers in Wolverhampton risk having their licences suspended or revoked . <p> The ANPR system , which oversees 15,400 traffic cameras across the UK , processes between 75 and 80 million number plate reads daily with a 97 per cent accuracy rate . However , this still results in approximately 2.4 million misread plates each day , further exacerbating concerns about enforcement reliability .

Ebi npa wa ! People can barely feed . Inflation is creating havoc on our salaries ! People are dying like flies because of depression . Too many suicides are taking place . @@118692737 <h> Ending gas flaring , another illusory exercise ? <p> In what appears as taking the recalcitrant bull by the horns , the House of Representatives has set the ball rolling in a bid to halt the dangerous practice of gas flaring in the oil producing communities in the Niger Delta region . A bill to rein in the monstrosity in Nigeria scaled a second reading last Thursday . <p> The sponsor of the bill and Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on Defence , Hon. Babajimi Benson , in presenting its general principles , described the move as representing " a decisive legislative intervention aimed at addressing the longstanding and damaging practice of gas flaring in Nigeria . " <p> He argued that the bill was firmly rooted in the constitutional obligation to protect the environment and promote sustainable development , with the overall objectives of mitigating the environmental , health , and economic impacts of gas flaring as well as aligning Nigeria 's oil and gas operations with international climate change commitments . <p> Entitled " Gas Flaring ( Prohibition and Enforcement ) Bill , 2024 " , Hon. Benson said it also seeks to prohibit the flaring and venting of natural gas , except in strictly regulated circumstances , while encouraging the utilisation of gas resources to foster economic growth and energy generation . The Bill also provides a robust framework for enforcement , monitoring , and the imposition of penalties to ensure compliance . <p> He lamented that the dangerous exercise had plagued Nigeria for decades , leading to severe environmental degradation , public health crises and colossal economic losses , stressing that environmentally , it has contributed to greenhouse gas emissions , global warming and acid rain , and above all , the climate challenges . <p> The renewed efforts at ending the menace of gas flaring may not excite many Nigerians . This is because it is not the first time the National Assembly will embark on this kind of mission . <p> As recently as 2019 , a resolution was passed by the 9th Senate for upward review of the penalty for breakers of the nation 's gas flaring laws . The upper chamber reached the resolution after consideration of a motion entitled : " The need to monitor the Nigerian Flare Commercialisation Programme Towards Ending Gas Flaring by 2020 " . <p> The motion , sponsored by Senator Betty Apiafi representing PDP Rivers West constituency , was intended to draw the attention of the Senate to the extant laws against flaring of associated natural gas in Nigeria . She lamented the manner in which the laws were being flaunted by international oil companies in the country . <p> According to Senator Apiafi , Section 3(1) of the Gas Re-injection Act introduced in 1984 states , " No company engaged in the production of oil and gas shall after January 1 , 1984 , flare gas produced in association with or without the permission in writing of the minister . " <p> She bemoaned the huge revenue loss due to relentless gas flares in the country , disclosing that in 2018 alone , figures revealed by the Nigeria National Petroleum Corporation ( NNPC ) indicated that the federal government lost about N197bn from a total of 215.9bn standard cubic feet of natural gas flared . <p> She further said , " Nigeria 's gas reserves are about three times the value of crude oil deposits with a value of about 202trn cubic feet of natural gas , but despite having the largest gas deposits in Africa , only about 25 per cent or less of these reserves are being produced . " <p> She noted that the lack of enforcement of the laws in previous years was thwarting the government 's projected deadline of 2020 to end routine associated gas flaring . <p> Currently , Nigeria ranks second to Russia and the largest in Africa on the global gas flaring index . Environmental experts have consistently urged the Nigerian government to caution all relevant emission defaulters to drastically limit gas emissions because of their fatal consequences on the environment . Nigeria is one of Africa 's top oil producers and the largest holder of natural gas reserves on the continent , with about 187trn cubic feet of proven gas reserves and 600scf of unproven gas reserves . <p> Curiously , Nigeria is not listed among the signatories to the treaty to end gas flaring at oil production fields globally by 2030 even when our own 2020 deadline had become a mirage four years ago . Four African countries , Angola , Cameroon , the Republic of Congo and Gabon , were among nine leading global crude oil producers that joined chief executives of major oil companies to endorse the " Zero Routine Flaring by 2030 " initiative . The initiative was launched in Washington DC , United States of America about eight or so years ago by the former United Nations Secretary-General , Ban Ki-Moon , and the ex-World Bank Group President , Jim Yong Kim . <p> It is regrettable to note that many oil companies in the country still flare their gas consequently polluting the environment with its attendant hazards . Many oil plants have remained recalcitrant and continued to run their operations leading to a waste of energy and money as well as putting the lives of the citizens in the oil producing communities at high risk . <p> Gas flaring has been a worrisome phenomenon which has defied a ban since the Gowon era till date . Many believe that systemic corruption is also a factor working against the move to achieve the deadlines for the elimination of the practice . <p> Reducing gas flare will undoubtedly make a significant contribution towards mitigating the horrific effects of climate change . The flared gas ought to be channeled towards improving Nigeria 's epileptic power sector . What is more , the present administration of Bola Ahmed Tinubu is preaching a shift to Compressed Natural Gas ( CNG ) -driven vehicles . There is , therefore , no better time to enforce the ban on the dangerous practice than now . <p> Finally , we urge the National Assembly to work closely with the executive arm to strengthen and/or enforce the extent laws on gas flaring rather than embarking on a fresh legislative exercise .

@@118692896 <p> The oceans , vast and unexplored , hold immense potential and challenges . In these depths , Remotely Operated Vehicles ( ROVs ) have become indispensable tools , driving progress in industries like offshore energy , marine science , and environmental management . Their integration into subsea remediation strategies represents a confluence of cutting-edge robotics and practical problem-solving , addressing some of the most pressing underwater challenges . <p> The Backbone of Subsea Operations : ROV Capabilities <p> ROVs are versatile , remotely controlled robots designed to perform complex tasks in the demanding conditions of deep-sea environments . Operating at depths where human divers can not reach , ROVs are equipped with state-of-the-art technology , enabling them to navigate , inspect , and intervene with precision . <p> Subsea remediation encompasses efforts to repair , restore , and mitigate issues affecting underwater environments or infrastructure . ROVs have become the cornerstone of these strategies due to their precision and adaptability . <p> Environmental Remediation Strategies <p> Oil Spill Response : In incidents like the Deepwater Horizon spill , ROVs have demonstrated their capability to address underwater leaks . They deploy dispersants , monitor the extent of spills , and operate containment equipment at extreme depths . <p> Leak Detection and Sealing : ROVs use sensors to pinpoint leaks in pipelines or wellheads . Equipped with sealing technologies , they can apply patches or clamps as temporary solutions until permanent repairs are feasible . <p> Innovations such as lightweight materials , increased battery efficiency , and modular designs are also enhancing the mobility and operational range of ROVs . Collaborative efforts between industry leaders and research institutions are pushing the boundaries of what ROVs can achieve , making them even more indispensable for subsea work . <p> Future Prospects <p> As global reliance on underwater resources grows , ROVs will become even more integral to subsea operations . Their role in emerging sectors like deep-sea mining , renewable energy , and climate change mitigation is expected to expand . Simultaneously , advancements in AI and sensor technology will enhance their autonomy and effectiveness . <p> The future of subsea remediation lies in the hands of ROVs , which offer scalable , safe , and sustainable solutions to humanity 's underwater challenges . By continuing to innovate and collaborate , industries and governments can ensure the health of marine ecosystems while meeting the demands of infrastructure development . <p> Conclusion <p> ROVs are not merely tools -- they are transformative agents , driving progress in underwater exploration and remediation . Their capabilities epitomize the union of technology and environmental stewardship , ensuring a sustainable future beneath the waves . 
@@118693232 <p> For the people of Ebe , Nsude , Nachi and Umulumgbe , all in Udi Local Government Council of Enugu State they are currently living with a ticking time bomb . <p> For close to a decade now , they have been living in palpable fear due to frequent collapse of abandoned coal mines in their communities , thereby leading to loss of expanse of land and huge economic trees . <p> WITHIN NIGERIA gathered that the worst hit community is Nsude , where residents have been living in trepidation , even as many youths have continued to express fear of further collapse of their farmlands . <p> Investigation by WITHIN NIGERIA revealed that coal mining started in Enugu State , particularly in the Nsude area , as early as in the 1920s following the coal discovery in 1909 . <p> Enugu coal miners in the early 80s <p> However , the Nsude drift opened six years later . The Enugu mine 's operations and others in the country were merged into a new corporation in 1950 : the Nigerian Coal Corporation . The NCC was tasked with exploiting coal resources , and held a monopoly on coal mining , production , and sales until 1999 . <p> Further checks showed that Nigeria 's coal industry suffered a blow in the 1950s when oil was discovered . Up until this point , the Nigerian Railway Corporation was the largest consumer of coal in the country . <p> However , after the discovery of oil , the railway corporation began to replace its coal burning trains with diesel-powered engines . An additional negative impact came when the Electricity Corporation of Nigeria began converting its power generation equipment from coal to diesel and gas as well . <p> The Nigeria Civil War also negatively impacted coal production ; many mines were abandoned during the war . Following the war , production never completely recovered and coal production levels were erratic . <p> It was discovered that attempts at mechanising production ended badly , as both the implementation and maintenance of imported mining equipment proved troublesome , and hurt production . After the civil war , the Nigerian coal industry has not been able to return to its peak production in the 1950s and even as the demand for the coal has continued to take a nose dive . <p> Further investigation showed that in 1999 , the NCC lost its monopoly over the Nigerian coal industry as the Obasanjo government allowed private companies to begin operating coal fields in joint ventures with the NCC , with an eventual goal of completely selling off the NCC 's assets to private investors . The Nigerian government planned to sell 40 per cent to private investors and 20 per cent to the Nigerian public , while retaining 40 per cent . <p> One of the abandoned coal mines <p> Consequent upon this , in 2002 , work stopped at the NCC-operated mines . In 2003 , the Nigerian government announced plans to create a technical advisory committee that would be tasked with reviving Nigeria 's coal industry . <p> By 2004 , the technical committee had still not issued their report , and the NCC found itself almost bankrupt . To raise funds , it began to sell off some of its assets in an attempt to pay off its mounting debts , including salaries owed to its employees , which WITHIN NIGERIA findings showed ran into billions of naira . <p> As the situation continued to become worse , the Enugu State Government protested the planned NCC privatisation and demanded the ability to consult with the Federal Government on any planned sale . <p> Following the above development , the coal mine sites were abandoned and subsequently deteriorated to the point of sliding , with mounting debt and environmental degradation . <p> Nsude community in palpable fear <p> In any case , following the reported case of collapse of the farmlands in the area , people of the area have become despondent . The most disturbing part of it is that it is becoming worse every year . @@118704157 <h> AFEX wants to improve food security across Africa <p> Ayodeji Balogun 's life 's work is driven by a singular passion : to bolster food security across the African continent . As a pioneering force in the region 's agricultural development , he co-founded AFEX , a revolutionary agricultural , finance , and technology-based exchange . Since its inception in 2014 , AFEX has made a profound impact , supporting over 500,000 smallholder farmers , processing over 500,000 metric tons of grain , and generating a turnover of over $300 million . Currently operational in three African countries , AFEX ambition is to extend its reach to several countries on the continent over the next decade . This strategic expansion is driven by the identification of unique opportunities in the agricultural market and the selection of trade hubs that will facilitate seamless intra-African trade . At its core , AFEX is committed to enabling efficient trade coordination across the continent , ultimately bridging the gap between Africa and the global market . As AFEX continues to drive transformative change in Africa 's agricultural landscape , Ayodeji Balogun 's unwavering dedication to food security and economic empowerment serves as a powerful catalyst for growth , innovation , and prosperity with Onome Amawhe . <p> Can you give us an overview of AFEX ? <p> We started AFEX in 2014 with a resounding vision from our founding investors : to unlock capital for the smallest unit of business in Africa -- smallholder farmers . Enmeshed in that vision was a quest to contribute to food security in Africa and to explore the commodity exchange model as a path to efficient and inclusive trade . <p> As a business , we have recorded a number of wins over the years . We especially hold dear our impact towards producers , and we have reached over 500,000 farmers over our operational locations since we started up . We have also unlocked over $400 million in financing for the agriculture sector on the continent during that period . <p> Today we are in 3 African countries , with a timeline to hit 10 total countries over a 10-year timeline . Our goal is to be a fundamental engine for intra-Africa trade coordination and make it truly seamless for Africa to trade across borders and ultimately for the rest of the world to trade with Africa . <p> Food insecurity deals with questions of access and affordability . It 's a complex mix of challenges that make it impossible to get sufficient , safe , and nutritious food to meet dietary needs and live healthy , and it most definitely is a problem that require a complex web of players collaborate to solve . <p> What makes Africa vulnerable to food insecurity ? <p> We have produced more people than the food we will use to feed them . Our value creation in agriculture has declined because we processed more food in decades past than we do today . This is a multiplier effect that has made the sector almost a poverty center . It is nearly an ill fate to be born by a smallholder farmer on the continent because immediately opportunities are not available for you . <p> Also , we have taken agriculture as a means of poverty eradication , and the result of that approach to agriculture has been creating fewer poor farmers . <p> The underlying thing is still that they are poor farmers . We have not created wealthy farmers as a continent over the last 3/4 decades . The last time we made wealthy farmers was in the early eighties , when we started seeing the continent 's entire market infrastructure collapse . Three decades after that , all farmers have remained poor . If you look at our production of food per capita , it has declined significantly . <p> To what extent do the food production and distribution systems in Africa reflect local needs , culture , and conditions ? <p> We have families who are into their third generation of farming , handing down knowledge from generation to generation , but also increasingly extension support programs are coming in to teach more modern and adaptable techniques . So it really is a mix , just as it should be . The big change that needs to happen across most African societies is the departure from the idea of agriculture as a core subsistence activity . More farmers treating agriculture as a business and plugging in to the networks that support that are vital for us . <p> How are food systems influencing and being impacted by climate change ? <p> In Nigeria , for example , smallholder farmers are experiencing climate disasters , including increased flooding as well as drought across some states , which is made worse by a lack of access to seasonal climate and weather information services . The implication of this is a significantly lower production volume across the agricultural value chain . Additionally , onethird of the world 's droughts occur in sub-Saharan Africa , with Ethiopia and Kenya currently enduring the worst droughts in at least four decades . <p> Torrential rains and floods are severely impacting countries such as Chad . <p> The time to innovate around Africa 's agriculture in the face of a climate crisis is now . <p> Through a range of initiatives , policymakers are implementing reforms to create an enabling environment for agriculture , focusing on sustainable practices and increased investment . A number of initiatives are being spearheaded from every corner , and we will continue to advocate for solutions that are scalable and that ensure that we can increase production , but we also continue to see the potential for increasing intra-Africa trade to plug demand and supply shortfalls across African countries . We were recently part of the founding members of the AfCFTA Association of Commodities Exchanges ( A-ACX ) after signing an MoU at the Intra-Africa Trade Fair in Cairo to promote intraAfrican trade in commodities , foster collaboration , and collectively address challenges and opportunities in the commodities exchange industry . <p> How much work is being done to strengthen African food security and improve their resilience to such shocks ? <p> When you are thinking about food security and agriculture , you are essentially thinking about a value chain . So many players have to play their part to ensure that food is available and accessible to everyone . <p> At the heart of the AFEX model is incentivizing these players to collaborate and work together to achieve our food security goals as a continent . So there is definitely a lot of work being done both in the public and private sectors . Most African governments practice a very active policy environment for the agriculture sector in their countries , and a number of innovative agribusinesses have emerged over the years . <p> What 's next for AFEX ? <p> At AFEX , our mission is to help Africa feed itself , and this is represented in our strategic goals to drive growth in key areas such as infrastructure , agriculture credit and financing , improved market access for the agriculture value chain , and stronger supply chains by coordinating across farmers , processors , and potentially consumers . <p> We believe in our ability to continue to unlock capital for the sector and run programs that are both impactful and commercially sustainable . Our commodities exchange model facilitates access to crucial resources such as financing , storage facilities , and other essential services , which ultimately enhance productivity and competitiveness . It is a model that is a core aspect of the food system transformation that Africa requires and that we are happy to deploy alongside other innovative players . <p> We also remain bullish that the solutions that we have developed are scalable across other African countries , and we will continue to expand across the continent in a way that allows us to enhance intra-Africa trade in key commodities , working alongside governments across Africa and other private sector players . <p> Business Day , established in 2001 , is a daily business newspaper based in Lagos . It is the only Nigerian newspaper with a bureau in Accra , Ghana . It has both daily and Sunday titles . It circulates in Nigeria and Ghana

@@118781713 <p> In this piece , ANOZIE EGOLE looks at the efforts of the Federal Government to comply with the directive of the International Maritime Organisation by ensuring a reduction in carbon emissions <p> The maritime industry is one of the largest contributors to global greenhouse gas emissions , accounting for around 2.5 per cent of total emissions worldwide . As the world continues to grapple with the impacts of climate change , industries across the globe are under increasing pressure to adopt more sustainable practices . Among these , the shipping sector has found itself in the spotlight , with governments , companies , and environmental organizations pushing for greener , more eco-friendly solutions . <p> Nigeria , a key player in the African maritime industry , stands at a crossroads . As the largest economy in Africa , the country 's maritime sector is vital to its economic growth , contributing approximately 5-6 per cent of Nigeria 's gross domestic product according to the National Bureau of Statistics . <p> However , the environmental impact of the sector is becoming a cause for concern . A significant portion of Nigeria 's shipping fleet continues to use high-polluting fuels , contributing to the country 's carbon footprint and hindering efforts to meet international climate goals . <p> This feature explores the push for green shipping in Nigeria , examining the policies , technological innovations , challenges , and opportunities in the quest for a more sustainable maritime industry . Drawing on reports from industry experts , government agencies , and environmental advocates , this article sheds light on the country 's journey toward embracing green shipping solutions . <p> What is green shipping ? <p> Green shipping is an umbrella term for practices and technologies designed to reduce the environmental impact of shipping activities . At its core , it focuses on minimising carbon emissions , reducing fuel consumption , and preventing marine pollution . Central to green shipping is the idea of decarbonising the industry by adopting cleaner fuels , implementing energy-efficient technologies , and improving waste management . <p> In 2018 , the International Maritime Organization , the global body that regulates shipping , set an ambitious target : to reduce total greenhouse gas emissions from ships by 50 per cent by 2050 , compared to 2008 levels . The IMO also set a target for zero emissions from ships by the end of the century . These targets set the tone for a global shift toward greener practices , compelling countries like Nigeria to take action . <p> Nigeria 's maritime sector , like many others , faces the challenge of reducing emissions and making the shift towards more sustainable practices . The push for green shipping in Nigeria is not just an environmental imperative ; it 's an economic and geopolitical opportunity . By adopting green shipping technologies and practices , Nigeria can not only improve its environmental record but also enhance its competitiveness in global trade , attract foreign investments , and create new jobs in green technologies . <p> Environmental impact on sector <p> Nigeria 's maritime sector is vast and critical to the country 's economy . The country 's ports , including Lagos Port Harcourt , and Calabar Ports , handle millions of tons of cargo annually , making Nigeria one of the most important maritime hubs in Africa . In 2021 alone , the Nigerian Ports Authority reported handling about 60 million metric tons of cargo , including oil , gas , and other essential goods . <p> However , the environmental impact of the maritime industry is substantial . The use of low-grade , sulfur-heavy marine fuels contributes to high levels of carbon dioxide emissions , particulate matter , and other harmful pollutants . <p> The carbon footprint of the sector is exacerbated by an ageing fleet that still operates on traditional fuels , which are less efficient and more harmful to the environment than newer technologies . <p> The Nigerian shipping industry is also plagued by inefficiencies , such as outdated vessel technologies and poor port infrastructure . The lack of eco-friendly ports , green ship technology , and energy-efficient vessels makes it difficult for the sector to reduce its environmental impact . Additionally , the country 's regulatory framework around environmental standards is often criticised for being weak and inconsistent . <p> What government can do <p> In recent years , Nigeria 's government has made significant strides toward promoting sustainability in its maritime sector . The government recognises that the maritime industry is not only essential for economic growth but also plays a crucial role in meeting the country 's international climate obligations , particularly under the Paris Agreement . <p> One of the key players in Nigeria 's green shipping transition is NIMASA , which has been instrumental in the development of policies to promote sustainable shipping . In 2020 , NIMASA launched its Green Shipping Agenda , aimed at reducing emissions from the country 's shipping activities . The agenda includes a variety of measures , such as , encouraging the use of low-sulfur fuels and exploring alternatives such as LNG and biofuels . Another one is the implementation of technologies to reduce fuel consumption , such as hull modifications , energy-saving devices , and optimised navigation routes . <p> The agency also improved port operations to reduce environmental impact , including the use of renewable energy sources , electric cargo handling equipment , and better waste management systems . Providing training programs to ensure that maritime operators and port workers are well-equipped to manage green shipping technologies and practices . <p> Furthermore , the Nigerian Ports Authority has introduced several initiatives to make Nigerian ports more sustainable . These initiatives include efforts to reduce emissions from port activities , integrate renewable energy into port operations , and improve waste management systems . <p> The Nigerian government has also signed on to international agreements that promote green shipping . As a member of the International Maritime Organization , Nigeria is committed to meeting the global targets for reducing emissions and transitioning to cleaner fuels . Additionally , the government is working to align its domestic regulations with the Marpol Annex VI standards , which set out regulations for the prevention of air pollution from ships . <p> However , despite these efforts , the country still faces challenges in implementing these policies effectively . Inadequate enforcement , lack of infrastructure , and limited funding for green technologies are significant barriers that need to be overcome . <p> A critical component of the green shipping movement in Nigeria is the adoption of innovative technologies . From cleaner fuels to advanced digital solutions , the maritime industry is increasingly turning to technology to drive sustainability . <p> One of the most promising avenues for reducing emissions in the Nigerian shipping industry is the use of cleaner fuels . Traditionally , ships have relied on heavy fuel oil , a high-sulfur , low-cost fuel that is a significant source of pollution . However , in line with global trends , Nigerian shipping companies are exploring alternative fuels such as LNG , biofuels , and ammonia . <p> In 2023 , NIMASA launched a pilot program to introduce LNG-powered vessels into the Nigerian fleet . LNG is a cleaner alternative to traditional marine fuels , emitting up to 25 per cent less carbon dioxide and significantly reducing sulfur and nitrogen oxide emissions . The pilot program , which is expected to run for several years , will test the viability of LNG as a sustainable fuel for Nigeria 's shipping industry . <p> In July 2023 , NIMASA stated Nigeria was in sync with IMO 's commitment to tackle climate change challenges associated with the shipping industry . <p> " Tackling climate change cutting GreenHouse Gas , emissions from ships including adoption of the revised IMO GHG Strategy was the focus at the just concluded 80th session of the Marine Environment Protection Committee of the International Maritime Organisation that took place in London . Nigeria 's Permanent Representative at the IMO Nigeria 's High Commissioner to the United Kingdom , Ambassador Sarafa Tunji Isola led other Nigerian delegates to participate in the session , where energy efficiency of ships and ballast Water Management among other topical issues were reviewed , " the statement read in part . <p> Additionally , some companies are working on biofuel projects that aim to reduce the reliance on fossil fuels in shipping operations . These projects are still in the early stages , but they represent a critical step toward diversifying Nigeria 's fuel mix and reducing emissions . <p> Energy efficiency is another area where Nigeria 's maritime industry can make significant improvements . Technologies such as air lubrication systems , wind-assisted propulsion , and fuel-saving devices can reduce fuel consumption and lower emissions . <p> For example , wind-assisted propulsion systems , such as large sails and kites , are being explored by Nigerian shipping companies . These systems work by harnessing wind energy to assist in ship propulsion , reducing the need for fuel . Though still in the experimental phase , these technologies hold great promise for reducing the fuel consumption of cargo ships , especially in Nigeria 's vast coastal waters . <p> The digital transformation of the maritime industry is also playing a key role in driving sustainability . Using big data , artificial intelligence , and the Internet of Things Nigerian shipping companies are improving fuel efficiency and reducing emissions . These technologies enable operators to optimize shipping routes , monitor vessel performance in real-time , and adjust operations to reduce fuel consumption . <p> Platforms such as SeaRates are being used by Nigerian shipping companies to calculate the most fuel-efficient routes for their vessels , helping them save costs and reduce emissions . Additionally , AI-powered predictive maintenance systems are being employed to ensure that vessels are running at optimal efficiency , further contributing to the green shipping agenda . <p> Challenges and opportunities <p> Despite the promising developments , the journey towards green shipping in Nigeria is not without its challenges . <p> Nigeria 's ports and shipping infrastructure are not yet equipped to handle the demands of green shipping . The lack of bunkering facilities for alternative fuels , such as LNG , is a significant barrier to adopting these cleaner fuels . <p> While Nigeria has made strides in aligning its regulations with international standards , enforcement remains weak . Without strong enforcement mechanisms , many shipping companies may not be incentivised to adopt green technologies . <p> Meanwhile , these have also presented some opportunities . One of the biggest opportunities for Nigeria lies in green financing . International institutions , such as the Green Climate Fund and the World Bank , are offering funding for green projects in developing countries , including Nigeria . These funds could help local shipping companies make the transition to cleaner technologies . <p> The shift toward green shipping could also create thousands of jobs in Nigeria . From green shipbuilding and retrofitting to research and development in alternative fuels , there are numerous opportunities for employment in the green shipping sector . <p> By adopting green shipping practices , Nigeria can position itself as a leader in sustainable maritime practices in Africa . This could open up new trade opportunities with countries that prioritise sustainability , attracting investment and improving Nigeria 's competitive position in global trade . <p> Government efforts <p> Precisely on June 6th , 2023 , the Federal Government through the NIMASA , announced the approval of the ratification of six maritime conventions and protocols that promote a cleaner marine environment , ship-breaking criteria , global standard for fishing crew , and response to oil pollution casualties . <p> In a statement , NIMASA mentioned that the approved instruments for ratification were the Hong Kong International Convention for Safe and Environmentally Sound Recycling of Ships 2009 ; the International Convention on Standards of Training Certification and Watchkeeping for Fishing Vessel Personnel ( STCW-F ) 1995 ; Protocol Relating to Intervention on the High Seas in Cases of Oil Pollution Casualties ( intervention protocol ) 1973 and the Protocol on Limitation of Liabilities for Maritime Claims 1996 . <p> " Others are the Protocol to the 1974 Athens Convention Relating to the Carriage of Passengers and their Luggage by Sea 2002 ; and the protocol of 2005 to the 1988 protocol to the Suppression of Unlawful Acts against the Safety of Fixed Platforms Located on the Continental Shelf ( SUA PROT 2005 ) . The approval , conveyed through the Federal Ministry of Transportation to the Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency(NIMASA) has kick-started Nigeria 's preparation to align with the global maritime community with respect to the protocols and conventions , " NIMASA stated in the statement . <p> The then Director General of NIMASA Dr. Bashir Jamoh , while thanking the Federal Government for the approval reassured industry players of the agency 's unflinching effort as designated authority to draw the gains of the various instruments closer to indigenous investors , professionals and all stakeholders in Nigeria . <p> Explaining the implication of each convention , said that the Hong Kong Convention is aimed at ensuring that ships , when being recycled after reaching the end of their operational lives , do not pose a risk to human health , safety , or the environment . <p> " STCW-F is a treaty that sets certification and minimum training requirements for crews of seagoing fishing vessels to promote the safety of life at sea and the protection of the marine environment , taking into account the unique nature of the fishing industry and the fishing working environment , " Jamoh said . <p> Jamoh added that the International Convention Relating to Intervention on the High Seas in Cases of Oil Pollution Casualties will see Nigeria taking action on the high seas to prevent , mitigate , or eliminate grave and imminent danger to Nigeria 's coastline or related interests from pollution or threat of pollution of the sea by oil spillage . <p> On the Convention of Limitation of Liability of Maritime Claims , Jamoh said it will provide for an unbreakable system of limiting liability where shipowners and sailors may limit their liability , except if it is proved that an incurred loss resulted from their personal act or omission or commission with the intent to cause loss , or recklessly and with the knowledge that such loss would probably happen . <p> The Athens Convention , according to Jamoh , establishes a regime of liability for damage suffered by passengers carried on a seagoing vessel . It places liability on the carrier for any loss or damage suffered by passengers where it is established to be the carrier 's fault . <p> He added that the Protocol for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts against the Safety of Fixed Platforms Located on the Continental Shelf ( SUA PROT ) will result in improved protection of oil platforms and sanction threats against such facilities which are critical to the country 's economic mainstay . <p> He further sought the cooperation of all stakeholders with NIMASA while hoping to engage with them at various stages of implementation in the near future . <p> Stakeholders speak <p> The Director General of the African Centre for Supply Chain and President of the Association of Outsourcing Professionals , Dr. Obiora Madu , believes that in as much as reducing green emissions is necessary , it is not really a priority to Nigeria . <p> He stated that though the government is doing something in that direction , meeting that target would be difficult for the country . <p> " I am going to be very honest with you , but the question I will ask you is , is that a priority for us as a country right now , the way the country is looking ? Is the Federal Government doing something ? Definitely , they are but meeting the target will probably be far from it . But the fact is that every country has priorities , " Madu said . <p> Madu who is also the Chief Executive Officer of Multimix Group , opined that the country is currently facing serious infrastructural problems . <p> " We have serious logistics infrastructural problems , we have economic challenges and the rest of them . And the government is battling with all this including the thing about sustainability , which is of course what this emission thing is all about to reduce the effect on the ozone layer . It is fantastic , but if you look at it , you will see that it has not gotten a stronghold , a foothold in Africa , " he said . <p> He stated that the reduction in greenhouse emissions is yet to have a strong footing in Africa due to several challenges . <p> " Not because it is not important but because there are more challenges , stronger challenges that exist . So the government is doing something , but the attention being paid to it is not like it is in Europe or elsewhere , the developed world . So my answer is yes , the government is doing something but there are more serious challenges that the government is encountering that will probably affect the amount of attention they are paying in that direction . I talked about logistics infrastructure . See our road , we do n't have rails , we do n't have rails , everything is still being carried on the road , tankers and the rest of them . These things could have gone by rail . So these are challenges in the logistic direction . Right now for me also , there are a lot of challenges policy-wise , because if you look at the blue economy , the ministry , the blue economy is so wide that so many other ministries are touched , " he said . <p> " So these are part of the challenges that have to be surmounted because , of course , this is the ministry that is looking at it . So hopefully people will point these things out , but whether it was properly thought out , I do n't know what to say . But the fact is that the ministry is supposed to be supervising a lot of the things that we 're talking about , because what you said relates to maritime transport . So it 's still this ministry and the agencies that are going to , and yet right now we are talking about policy , and so it will take a while for it to take root , " he said . <p> The Executive Director of Operations and Technical at Tantita Nigeria Limited , Captain Warredi Enisouh , said , " Naturally , the ships are supposed to declare their greeningness to the Nigerian Ports Authority and Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency . They may be doing so , but I 'm not too sure , " he said . <p> The President of the Alumni of the Federal College of Fisheries and Marine Technology , Captain Williams Ogunshakin , said that the major challenge affecting Nigeria 's fight to ensure emission reduction is corruption . <p> " The challenge we have is the challenge of all this corruption we are talking about . Because when we talk of flaring , we are talking about gases in the ocean . They are still floating to me , they are still flaring , though it has reduced , it has reduced currently , but they are still flaring , both in the sea and on land , they are still flaring . That is the highest killer of the ozone layer , " Ogunshakin stated . <p> " When you talk about the use of low sulfur oil , they are trying to make Nigerian vessels comply , that is why when they go to port , they come for inspection to show them the certificate you use in getting your fuel , " Ogunshakin continued . <p> He said that the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority is trying to inspect to ensure that vessels coming to the country are compliant . <p> " They are doing that , part of it . They will make sure every cargo that arrives in our port , comes for the analysis . They will come and take a sample of the product . They will tell you to wait , to wait until they come with their results . Because you know some of them bad , high sulfur content fuel to us . That is why the NMDPRA is doing that , " he said . <p> Conclusion <p> The push for green shipping in Nigeria is gaining momentum , driven by both environmental imperatives and economic opportunities . While the country faces significant challenges in adopting green technologies , the potential benefits ranging from cleaner air to enhanced competitiveness in global markets are too great to ignore . <p> The Nigerian government , regulatory bodies like NIMASA , and the private sector must continue to work together to overcome the obstacles that stand in the way of green shipping . By investing in cleaner fuels , energy-efficient technologies , and sustainable port operations , Nigeria has the potential to transform its maritime industry into a model of sustainability for the entire African continent . <p> As the world increasingly embraces green practices , Nigeria must navigate a path toward a sustainable maritime future one that balances economic growth with environmental stewardship . In doing so , the country can help chart a course for global shipping toward a cleaner , greener , and more sustainable future . <p> According to Madu , the government should have probably had a marine transport ministry if they must have it , " but create a blue economy commission because it 's going to be difficult for that new ministry to load it over older ministries . So at the end of the day , you are going to see , particularly in a situation where governments work in silos , collaborations do not exist . " <p> The Project Coordinator , African Maritime Art Exhibition , Mrs. Ezinne Azunna , said , " Much more can be done , I think that by the time we check the impacts of these challenges , we should be able to be telling ourselves the truth that we should n't be playing at this moment with issues of climate change and all that . So there is a whole lot to be done and we hope that government should show themselves more . I am aware that some paraststals have started developing stuff and that is a good step in the right direction . We must understand what the problem is and how to go about it . There are stipulated ways from IMO and other bodies . So it is on us to push this conversation . " <p> Anozie is a Chief Correspondent with PUNCH .
